title: Turning a day's results into the next day's plan
target: How to read a finished day in Supermarket Simulator and turn it into tomorrow's plan: the record the game keeps, the costs behind it, the standing it feeds, and the decisions that belong before the next day starts.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A day finished rather than paused halfway
The day's own screen or the shop computer to read it on
Some idea of the shop's current level and standing

steps.do: Read the finished day before you spend anything from it.
steps.because: the game keeps a daily record with a manager of its own, a screen of its own and a drawing step of its own, so the day can be read back rather than remembered (DailyStatisticsData, DailyStatisticsManager, DailyStatisticsScreen, DrawStatistics)

steps.do: Separate what came in from what the shop owes.
steps.because: recurring costs are a system of their own, with a manager, a container for the settings and a record for each expense (ExpensesManager, ExpensesSO, ExpensesData, ExpenseType)

steps.do: Check what was paid for you before counting the day as yours.
steps.because: bills can be settled automatically, and the game keeps a canvas showing what it paid with an entry per bill (AutoPaymentManager, AutoPaidBillsCanvas, BillItem)

steps.do: Read cleanliness as part of the result rather than a separate chore list.
steps.because: cleanliness is tracked against the shop's standing, so the state of the shop feeds the same standing the day is measured by (CleaningReputationManager)

steps.do: Look at the shop's level before planning what to buy.
steps.because: the shop's level is tracked apart from the money, and the licence and growth screens are organised around it (StoreLevelManager, currentStoreLevel, LicenseLayoutConfig, GrowthLayoutConfig)

steps.do: Decide whether tomorrow is a buying day or a mending day.
steps.because: what can be ordered is modelled as real objects rather than text rows, and a box carries a market price of its own, so a buying day has a price the game already knows (Order, OrderData, ProductSOs, BoxMarketPrice)

steps.do: Bank before you shop, and know what the shop is holding.
steps.because: the shop's money is held by a manager, with a networked manager in a shared shop and a listener for money objects in the room (MoneyManager, NetworkMoneyManager, RoomMoneyListener)

steps.do: Plan the tills before you plan the shelves.
steps.because: there is a checkout manager and more than one kind of checkout, so standing at a till is a decision the game models rather than an assumption (CheckoutManager, CheckoutType, AutomatedCheckout)

ending the day is an interaction of its own, the day cycle has a networked manager, and the shop's status is part of the shared state in a co-op shop (NextDayInteraction, NetworkDayCycleManager, StoreStatus, NetworkStoreStatus)

commonMistakes: Spending the day's takings before reading what the day actually owed.
Treating cleanliness as decoration when it feeds the standing the results are judged against.
Ordering stock before checking what the shop's level and licences allow.
Planning a solo day in a shop that is shared with other players.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
